newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah edges lower on liquidity, fixing.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah edges lower on liquidity, fixing.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah edged lower against the dollar in moderate late trading on Thursday after the central bank raised its fixing, dealers said.
One Japanese bank dealer said both offshore and local operators were seen bidding for the dollar after the central bank depreciated the rupiah by another point.
"It's a kind of adjustment but I think the dollar was oversold. Ample liquidity also helped it rebound," he said.

Dealers said spot dollars were traded below the 2,340 level before fixing but it rose to a high of 2,340.15/40.25 at 0945 GMT from an opening of 2,339.5/40.5. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,339.0/39.1 and 2,338.3/38.5, respectively.
They said the fixing did not surprise the market because it was anticipated, partly due to the recent depreciation of the rupiah by at least three points in a week by the central bank.

Worries over a possible tightening on Friday due to the liquidity report and weekly tax payments caused tom/next rates to rise to a high of 1.5/1.7 points, but sustained ample liquidity and the absence of overnight papers (SBIs) sent it down to 1.0/1.2.
"This may indicate that people are expecting similar ample condition on Friday," one local bank dealer said.
Overnight swap was at 0.20/0.25. Overnight money fell to a low of six percent before closing at eight percent.
Ample liquidity was caused by the central bank's injection of more than two trillion rupiah in the morning. The central bank only offered SBIs longer than three and four days.
Dealers said trading in the swap market was brisk but the rates were relatively stable. Only one-month swap edged up.
One-month swap was at 15.25/15.50, two at 31.0/32.0, three at 45.5/47.0 and six at 91.0/92.0 points.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention band to 2,339/2,531 and the conversion rate to 2,339/2,387.
